setup: Back and hips flat against the pad
Feet mid-plate, about hip to shoulder width
Press up, then release the safety catches
execution: Lower slowly, knees in line with your toes
Stop before your hips curl off the pad
faults: Don't let your lower back or hips peel off the pad
Don't lock your knees out hard at the top
Don't let your heels lift off the plate
Don't let your knees cave inward

notes: Learn where the machine's safety catches are before loading it. Re-engage them before you take your feet off the plate.
If the machine has adjustable stops, set them just below your lowest position.
Keep a slight bend in the knees at the top; don't lock them under load.
The logged load is the plates added. It isn't the true resistance, and numbers aren't comparable between machines.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view of a 45° plate-loaded leg press, rail rising to the right, camera at seat height. Figure reclined on the seat pad with feet on the sliding foot plate. Whole machine outline in frame.

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Reclined on the pad, lower back and hips flat on it. Feet flat in the middle of the plate about hip to shoulder width. Legs nearly straight with a small knee bend. Hands on the side handles.

keyPositions.label: Halfway
keyPositions.describe: Foot plate halfway down the rail. Knees bending in line with the toes. Feet flat, hips and back still on the pad.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Knees bent about 90°. Thighs coming toward the chest, but hips and lower back still flat on the pad (tailbone not curling up). Heels flat on the plate.

guideBrief.barPath: Foot plate moves along the fixed 45° rail; feet fixed to the plate; hips fixed to the seat
emphasise: Hips and lower back stay on the pad at the bottom
Feet stay flat on the plate throughout
Knees stay slightly bent at the top

uncertain.note: Hip angles depend on the machine's seat-back angle, which varies by model. Treat them as drawing targets only.
Safety catches and stops differ between machine models. The advice is general practice, not from the cited sources.
Limited to plate-loaded machines on purpose. Selector-pin seated leg presses are a separate entry (machine-seated-leg-press) so stack and plate histories don't mix.
